title: CloudTrail + Config + Access Analyzer
format: Scenario → best service → why not the others

questions.question: A security team needs to investigate which IAM user deleted an S3 object from a production bucket three days ago. Which service should they use first?
You need continuous evaluation of whether any S3 bucket in the account currently allows public read access. Which service is purpose-built for this?
A company with 20 AWS accounts needs a single dashboard showing Config compliance status across all accounts and regions. What is the best approach?

options.A: Enable a multi-Region CloudTrail in each account
options.C: Enable GuardDuty in the management account only

questions.question: An auditor requires proof that CloudTrail log files have not been tampered with after delivery to S3. Which CloudTrail feature addresses this?
You discover an S3 bucket policy that grants s3:GetObject to Principal "*". Which tool identifies whether this resource is accessible from outside your AWS account?
Which statement correctly distinguishes CloudTrail and AWS Config?

options.A: CloudTrail records resource configuration; Config records API calls
options.B: CloudTrail records API activity; Config records resource configuration history and rule compliance
options.C: Both services require GuardDuty to be enabled first
options.D: Config replaces CloudTrail for IAM audit requirements

questions.question: An EC2 instance is communicating with a known command-and-control IP address. Which service would most likely generate this finding?
You want a unified view of findings from GuardDuty, Inspector, and Config in one place with severity scoring. Which service should you enable?
A team wants automated malware scanning of EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances when suspicious behavior is detected. Which GuardDuty feature addresses this?

After enabling AWS Config, the dashboard shows globalskiatlas.com bucket as NON_COMPLIANT on S3_BUCKET_PUBLIC_READ_PROHIBITED, but the static site works correctly via CloudFront. What is the most accurate interpretation?

options.A: The site is hacked — CloudFront is serving malicious content
options.B: Config is broken because the bucket must be private for CloudFront
options.C: The bucket policy allows public read, which violates the rule; the site may still work if public read is intentional (OAC migration would fix compliance)
options.D: CloudTrail will automatically fix the bucket policy overnight
